solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Copper gets stuck into pissed messenger

indicators.note: Something stuck into another thing ends up inside it, so the first piece goes within the second.

parts.note: merry is British slang for tipsy
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer lays into a drunk courier.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman in the scene, but it is the metal; Mercury was the messenger of the Roman gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury carried messages for the Roman gods, so his name stands for a messenger.

clue.text: (& 18dn.) Choice oaths … little chance they'll materialise?

definitions.note: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: it says what such pledges are notorious for.

parts.note: a choice made by voters
oaths are solemn vows or undertakings

explanation.surface: A cynic's take on the pledges politicians make at the ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a phrase about swearing, but each is a plain synonym, and together they name the pledges voters rarely see kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Election promises are proverbially made to win votes and then quietly dropped.

clue.text: Automatic pass? That's sort of pants

parts.note: an automatic is a car with automatic gears
to have a pass at something is to have a go at it

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an automatic exam pass as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is British slang for rubbish, which is how the surface reads it; here it means trousers, as in cargo pants with big side pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo pants are loose trousers with large pockets, one sort of pants.

clue.text: Detached soldiers keep going after arse

indicators.note: What goes after something follows it, so this piece is written after the other one.

parts.note: the rear is the backside
to keep something is to guard it

explanation.surface: Soldiers who have broken away keep chasing someone's behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep reads as carry on in the surface, but it is a verb meaning protect; detached means sent apart from the main force.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard is a body of troops detached to protect the back of an army.

clue.text: Prick, at first somewhat rough, becomes demure

indicators.note: At first points to the start of the word, so only its opening letter is used.

parts.note: the first letter of Prick
rude means rough, and the -ish ending means somewhat

explanation.surface: A rough sort of man turns coy.
explanation.walkthrough: Prick reads as an insult for a man, but only its first letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A prudish person is excessively modest, and demure means modest or reserved.

clue.text: Bullet scraped Rees-Mogg's backside off

indicators.note: A backside is the rear end, so it picks the last letter of the name.

parts.note: ground, the past of grind, can mean scraped

indicators.note: Off means taken away, so that letter is removed.

parts.note: the last letter of Rees-Mogg, removed from the front of GROUND

explanation.surface: A bullet grazes the rear of the Tory politician Jacob Rees-Mogg.
explanation.walkthrough: Scraped reads as grazed by the bullet, but it is the past tense of grind; Jacob Rees-Mogg is a Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the military sense: one shot's worth of ammunition is called a round.

clue.text: Complaint about senior party lackeys starts to generate anger

indicators.note: About means around, so the complaint wraps round the other letters.
Starts are the beginnings of words, so the first letter of each is taken.

parts.note: a complaint is an illness
the first letters of party and lackeys, placed after DIS
surface padding: its S appears to double with the S already in DISEASE

explanation.surface: A grievance about the underlings of a party grandee stirs up fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaint reads as a grievance but means an illness here. The S of senior seems to double with the S already in DISEASE, so the parse is looser than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: displeasing someone and angering them are the same act, give or take intensity.

clue.text: Erection doubtful after second time

indicators.note: After means following, so this piece comes behind the others.

parts.note: s is the standard abbreviation for second
t is the standard abbreviation for time
iffy means doubtful or uncertain

explanation.surface: A man's second attempt at arousal proves unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: Second and time read as a second go, but each is just its standard one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: the answer is British slang for the same thing.

clue.text: se 13ac.
Public-spirited, one gets into kinky catsuit with left and right openings

indicators.note: Kinky means twisted, so the letters are rearranged.

parts.note: one as the Roman numeral I
the word itself goes into the mix

indicators.note: Openings are the beginnings of words, so only the first letters are taken.

parts.note: the first letters of left and right

explanation.surface: Someone does a good deed by squeezing into a fetish catsuit with side slits.
explanation.walkthrough: Openings looks like slits in the catsuit, but it takes the first letters of left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruistic means selflessly concerned for others, which is what public-spirited people are.

clue.text: Social media mischief-maker: "Reform leader should be in charge"

indicators.note: The leader of a word is its first letter.

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge

indicators.note: What should be in something goes inside it.

parts.note: the first letter of Reform

explanation.surface: An online agitator demands that Reform's leader take control.
explanation.walkthrough: Reform is the British party Reform UK, and in charge reads as running things; charge is a fee here.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll posts provocative messages online to stir up trouble.

clue.text: Keep what Rishi never had over his party?

definitions.meaning: a keep is the fortified tower of a castle

definitions.text: what Rishi never had over his party?
definitions.meaning: a firm grip, which Rishi Sunak never had on the Conservatives; split the answer in two to see it

explanation.surface: A jibe at Rishi Sunak's weak grip on the Conservative Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a castle's inner tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold is a fortified place, just as a keep is.

clue.text: (& 9ac.) Lords member, jailbird taking piss

indicators.note: Taking means holding on to, so the jailbird takes the other piece inside.

parts.note: a jailbird can be a prisoner serving the longest sentence, in for the rest of their natural span
a milder word for the same thing

explanation.surface: A convicted member of the House of Lords is mocked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the piss is British slang for mocking, which the surface suggests; here piss is simply urine.
explanation.definitionFit: A life peer sits in the House of Lords for life, without passing the title on.

clue.text: Eye feature — wow, almost, almost upon us!

indicators.note: Almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the next piece is dropped.

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
something almost upon us is near; the preceding instruction cuts its R

explanation.surface: An excited cry about an eye that is nearly arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: The first almost is the instruction and the second belongs to the phrase almost upon us, which means near.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the transparent front layer of the eye.

clue.text: Get it on madly with heartless Alice then pull off

indicators.note: Madly means wildly, so the letters are rearranged.
Heartless means with the middle removed, so only the outer letters remain.

parts.note: the words themselves go into the mix
Alice without its middle letters

explanation.surface: A frantic sexual encounter with a cold-hearted Alice, followed by withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pull off suggests withdrawal in the surface, but here it means to succeed in, as in negotiating an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate an obstacle is to get past it successfully, to pull it off.

clue.text: After large double, a bloke gets end away — beast!

indicators.note: Double means twice, so the letter is written two times.
Gets end away means loses its last letter.

parts.note: l is the abbreviation for large, doubled
the letter itself
a bloke is a man, and his final N goes

explanation.surface: After a stiff drink a man has sex and is branded an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting your end away is British slang for having sex; here it just means losing the last letter. A double is a double measure of spirits in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American animal, a beast.

clue.text: Liz Cheney to Trump: "Hence army needs mobilising"

definitions.note: The definition is an example: Liz Cheney, the Republican who led the Capitol riot inquiry, is Trump's arch-enemy.

indicators.note: To mobilise is to set in motion and rearrange, so the letters are shuffled into order.

parts.note: the words themselves are the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Liz Cheney tells Trump that troops must be called up.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words look like Cheney's speech, but they are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheney became Trump's fiercest Republican opponent, his arch-enemy.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Faint insult about "Vacuous Davey!"

indicators.note: About means turned round, so the insult is written backwards.
Vacuous means empty, so the inside of the name is emptied out and only its outer letters stay.

parts.note: a dig is a sly insult
Davey with its middle removed

explanation.surface: A feeble jibe at Ed Davey, the Liberal Democrat leader, calling him empty-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: Faint reads as describing the insult; it is the definition, meaning dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling giddy is feeling faint and dizzy.

clue.text: The very old blokes' country

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the, as in ye olde tea shoppe
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A land that belongs to elderly men.
explanation.walkthrough: The very old reads as elderly people, but it asks for the archaic form of the.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a country in the south of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Conservative leader sheer crap, as seen on TV

definitions.note: The definition names the answer as a television title: Cheers was the American sitcom set in a Boston bar.

indicators.note: Crap means badly made, so the letters of sheer are jumbled.
The leader of a word is its first letter.

parts.note: the first letter of Conservative
the word itself, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory leader spouting utter rubbish on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheer crap reads as utter nonsense, but crap is the instruction to rearrange sheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers was a long-running TV sitcom, so the answer is something seen on TV.

clue.text: Speedy Penny has old colleague grabbed by balls

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny

indicators.note: What is grabbed by something is held inside it.

parts.note: balls is British slang for nonsense, which is rot
an MP, Penny Mordaunt's former fellow member of Parliament, goes inside ROT

explanation.surface: Penny Mordaunt, the Tory politician, and a former colleague caught in a compromising grip.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny reads as Penny Mordaunt, who lost her seat in 2024, so an MP is now her old colleague; here Penny is just P.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means quick or without delay, so speedy.

clue.text: Trump Jr. put Republican in club?

definitions.note: The definition is a jibe by example: the question mark flags Donald Trump Jr. as a spoilt child.

indicators.note: Put tells you to place the letter somewhere.
In says where: inside the other piece.

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Donald Trump's son enrols a Republican in a private club.
explanation.walkthrough: Club reads as a members' club, but it is something to hit with.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a spoilt, badly behaved child, the setter's view of Trump's son.

clue.text: Adder, minute, say — a disappointing British seasonal event

definitions.note: The definition is a jokey description: British summers are famously wet and short.

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, an adder
a minute is an example of time, as say signals

explanation.surface: A snake and a tiny thing mark the usual letdown of a British summer.
explanation.walkthrough: Adder looks like the snake, but it is one who adds up, a summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Summertime is the summer season, which in Britain is proverbially a disappointment.

clue.text: Sex cut short — contraceptive leak

indicators.note: Cut short means trimmed, here all the way back to the first letter.

parts.note: Sex reduced to its first letter
the pill is the oral contraceptive

explanation.surface: A hurried encounter and a failed contraceptive.
explanation.walkthrough: Leak sits at the end of the surface as the pill failing, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: liquid that escapes has both leaked and been spilt.

clue.text: Trump at first, almost without help, gets the crooked finger

indicators.note: At first points to the opening letter of the word.
Almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes.

parts.note: the first letter of Trump
alone means unaided; its final E is dropped

explanation.surface: Donald Trump, acting alone, gets the middle finger.
explanation.walkthrough: The crooked finger suggests a gesture at Trump, but a talon is a bird's hooked claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a hooked claw, a bird of prey's crooked finger.

clue.text: Cyclops's game? Edginess

parts.note: Cyclops is the setter, so from the setter's mouth this is I'm
patience is a card game for one player

explanation.surface: The setter wonders what his favourite pastime is.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for I, and the possessive 's is read as the is of I'm; patience is the British name for solitaire.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: restless irritation at waiting is what edginess names.

clue.text: Sunak's top tip is to be cushioned by fortune having done this electorally

definitions.note: The definition asks what Sunak did at the ballot box, so the answer is the past participle he suffered.

indicators.note: The top tip of a word is its very first letter.

parts.note: your lot is your fortune in life

indicators.note: Cushioned by means surrounded, so the letter sits inside the other piece.

parts.note: the first letter of Sunak

explanation.surface: Rishi Sunak's best advice is to have a soft landing after being defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunak led the Conservatives to heavy defeat in the 2024 general election, so this is what he did electorally.
explanation.definitionFit: Having lost an election is what Sunak did in 2024.

clue.text: Arrestee pleaded "nursing big erection"

indicators.note: Nursing means holding close, so the answer is held within the words before it.

parts.note: the letters run across arreSTEE PLEaded

explanation.surface: Someone under arrest explains his condition in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Erection reads as a bodily state, but it means a tall building here.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a tall church spire, a big structure erected.

clue.text: Many G&Ts spilled into tumbler

indicators.note: Spilled letters are scattered, so they land in a new order.

parts.note: G&T is gin and tonic, and the ampersand is dropped

explanation.surface: Lots of gin and tonics poured into a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: Tumbler looks like a drinking glass, but it is someone who does somersaults.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is an acrobat, and a gymnast performs the same moves.
